1. [Reminder service contract not yet defined] There is no existing `ReminderService` / `ReminderScheduler` interface in the current tree, but `ReminderSettingsView` currently persists settings directly via `@AppStorage` (`Recall/Features/Settings/ReminderSettingsView.swift`), so integrator must introduce a single ownership point to avoid dual settings sources.

2. [State ownership conflict risk] `ReminderSettingsView` is already writing AppStorage keys (`Recall.RemindersEnabled`, `Recall.ReminderHour`, `Recall.ReminderMinute`) as the runtime source of truth; a new service layer must either consume and mutate these same keys or replace this model, otherwise toggle/time can drift out of sync.

3. [API drift risk] The proposed scheduler snippet uses `notificationSettings(for: .default)` and older-style branching (`#available(iOS 14.0, *)`), while this codebase is iOS 17+ and already uses `notificationSettings()` in app UI code (`Recall/Features/Settings/ReminderSettingsView.swift`), so compile/behavior incompatibility is likely unless reconciled.

4. [Hardcoded domain data] `ReminderService` proposal hardcodes `dueCount = 10` (and in tests) despite UI copy claiming dynamic due-card count; this breaks correctness immediately when reminders are actually wired to real review data.

5. [Unused/ignored contract input] `setReminder(... deckID:)` receives `deckID` but doesn’t use it, while `Deck` model already has reminder fields (`reminderHour`, `reminderMinute`) (`Recall/Data/RecallModels.swift`), creating a clear mismatch if per-deck reminders are expected.

6. [No resync path for time UI] The added time picker persists value only in AppStorage; changing time does not currently call a scheduler refresh path, so the new `ReminderService` won’t reflect user edits unless `ReminderPermissionModel` is integrated with it.

7. [Testability / file mismatch] The proposed `ReminderServiceTests.swift` (currently missing) references mock-like behavior on non-mockable value types, so a protocol/`actor`/interface extraction will be required before tests can validate scheduling/permission flows.
